rows.selection_reason: Existing evidence is nonexistent, so the first experiment should test the most impactful design choice: multimodal integration. This configuration tests combining RNA (pca_n2000) and image (resnet50) data with simple concatenation fusion, which clarifies whether multimodal approaches outperform single-modality baselines. It balances exploration by testing a foundational multimodal setup while avoiding overfitting to complex hyperparameters.

The existing evidence shows that config_016 (multimodal, singleprofile, concat fusion) achieves moderate accuracy (0.5266). This experiment tests whether changing the fusion method from 'concat' to 'weighted' improves performance, a critical design choice in multimodal models. It directly addresses uncertainty about fusion strategies while building on the previous setup, balancing exploitation of the current model architecture with exploration of key hyperparameters.

Existing evidence shows that for singleprofile, concat fusion (config_016) slightly outperforms weighted fusion (config_017). However, multiprofile settings have not been tested yet. This experiment tests multiprofile with avgpool aggregation and concat fusion, which will clarify whether profile setting and aggregation method significantly impact performance. It balances exploration of key design choices (profile setting) with reuse of proven components (pca_n2000, resnet50, concat fusion).

Existing evidence shows that config_018 (multimodal, multiprofile, pca_n2000, resnet50, avgpool, concat) achieves the highest validation accuracy (0.6186). This experiment tests changing the fusion method from 'concat' to 'weighted' while keeping other components the same, to determine if weighted fusion improves performance. It directly builds on the top-performing configuration, testing a key design choice (fusion method) with minimal changes, balancing exploitation of strong evidence and exploration of critical parameters.

Existing evidence shows that multimodal models with multiprofile, avgpool aggregation, and weighted fusion (e.g., config_019) achieve the highest accuracy. This experiment tests whether replacing the image encoder (resnet50 → imagenet_vit_l) further improves performance, clarifying the importance of image encoder choice. It is the best next step as it directly explores a key design decision (image encoder) with minimal changes to the proven high-performing baseline.

Existing evidence shows that multimodal models with multiprofile, avgpool aggregation, and weighted fusion (e.g., config_019) achieve the highest accuracy so far. This experiment tests whether switching the RNA encoder from pca_n2000 to scvi_n200 (a more sophisticated encoder) in this high-performing setup improves accuracy, clarifying the importance of RNA encoder choice. It balances exploitation of the current best configuration with exploration of a key design decision.

Existing evidence shows that multiprofile settings and scvi_n200 RNA encoder significantly improve performance (config_031: 0.6776 accuracy). This experiment tests transformer aggregation (a key design choice not yet tested with scvi_n200) in a multimodal multiprofile setup, which could clarify whether transformer aggregation outperforms avgpool in this context. It balances exploitation of proven components (scvi_n200, multiprofile) with exploration of a critical architectural decision.

Existing evidence shows that multimodal models with scvi_n200 RNA encoder, resnet50 image encoder, and transformer aggregation achieve high accuracy (config_032: 0.6878). This experiment tests the same RNA/image encoders and aggregation but with weighted fusion instead of concat, clarifying whether fusion type is a critical factor. It builds on the promising direction of scvi_n200 + transformer and avoids redundant tests of lower-performing configurations.

Existing evidence shows that using scvi_n200 RNA encoder, transformer aggregation, and weighted fusion (config_033) achieves high performance. This experiment tests whether replacing resnet50 with the stronger imagenet_vit_l image encoder further improves performance while maintaining the effective aggregation/fusion strategy. It directly addresses the critical design choice of image encoder quality in multimodal settings.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal models with multiprofile settings, scvi_n200 RNA encoder, and imagenet_vit_l image encoder achieve the highest validation accuracy (0.724989). This experiment tests whether using scgpt RNA encoder with the same image encoder, aggregation, and fusion method could further improve performance, clarifying the importance of RNA encoder choice. It is the best use of the next experiment as it directly compares a promising RNA encoder (scgpt) against the current top performer (scvi_n200) under the same optimal configuration.
